article.title: The Dominican Government Uses Zionism to Whitewash Trujillo
article.author: Simón Rodríguez
article.content: On August 24, the Dominican government announced its adherence to the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance’s (IHRA) definition of antisemitism. President Luis Abinader , a businessman of Lebanese descent, made the announcement at the opening ceremony of the Sixth Latin American Forum Against Antisemitism,held in Santo Domingo by the US-based Combat Antisemitism Movement (CAM). Abinader also promised to invest 50 million pesos (approximately US$852,000) in the construction of a Jewish museum in Sosúa, in the north of the country, where 747 European Jewish refugees settled during the 1940s. The foreign ministry statement announcing Abinader’s decision included a defense of the Trujillo dictatorship (1930–1961) as a supposed opponent of discrimination, hatred, and religious intolerance. Rafael Trujillo, whose dictatorship was fanatically racist, perpetrated a genocide against the Haitian population along the Dominican border between late 1937 and early 1938 and was obsessed with “whitening” the Dominican Republic, whose overwhelming majority was and continues to be of African descent. The government’s invocation of Trujillo’s legacy is key to understanding its real motivation in pledging allegiance to the IHRA definition of antisemitism. The Dominican government is an unconditional ally of Israel’s apartheid regime. One of its first measures upon coming to power was a statement in 2020 in favor of establishing the Dominican embassy in Jerusalem. In 2023, the Santo Domingo International Book Fair had the Israeli embassy as guest of honor. An agreement with Mekorot, Israel’s state-owned water company, to design a national water management plan was signed, and there is also Israeli cooperation with the Dominican office for the technification of irrigation. President Abinader has drawn inspiration from the Israeli wall system that encloses Gaza and Palestinian communities in the West Bank for his own border wall with Haiti, and he has relied on the purchase of Israeli weapons to drive the largest arms buildup in the country since the Trujillo dictatorship. The government also relies on Israeli technologies for internal repression, having used Pegasus spyware against a journalist who was investigating corruption. The current Dominican government’s claim to oppose discrimination runs counter to all evidence. It has refused to introduce legislation against hate crimes and incitement to racial or religious hatred. The Penal Code, which took effect in August 2026, defines the crime of discrimination but effectively eliminates any penalty for discriminatory actions justified on religious grounds or in which the legitimate exercise of a legal authority is invoked, which amounts to the legalization of discrimination. The 1943 law banning the Vodou religion, enacted by Trujillo, remains in effect and is used to persecute Afro-Dominicans and Haitians. Meanwhile, a 1962 law prohibiting the glorification of Trujillo and Trujilloism is not enforced. Neofascist paramilitary groups that praise Trujillo, Benito Mussolini, and Adolf Hitler operate openly and collaborate with the police to repress the Left and Haitian communities. In this context, Abinader, like Trujillo, claims to oppose antisemitism in order to whitewash and further his own racist agenda. In Service of Genocide CAM, which promoted the Dominican adoption of the IHRA working definition of antisemitism, is linked to the Israeli foreign ministry. Both its CEO, Sacha Roytman-Dratwa, and its editor in chief, Barney Breen-Portnoy, have worked in communications for the Israel Defense Forces. Senior Israeli officials , such as the country’s current president, Isaac Herzog, have served on its advisory board. The organization has promoted the criminalization of the slogan “From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free,” following the example of the Austrian government in 2023. The Jewish Council of Australia has considered CAM’s summits on antisemitism to be part of an effort to silence criticism of Israel’s genocide against the Palestinian people by equating it with antisemitism. In its statements, CAM has defended Israel’s military actions in Gaza, describing them as an exercise in self-defense . Conversely, the International Association of Genocide Scholars has described Israel’s actions and policies in Gaza as crimes against humanity and war crimes and has stated that they meet the legal definition of genocide. Among the organizations that initially affiliated with CAM was the Clarion Project , an anti-Islam lobby that has been classified by the Southern Poverty Law Center as a hate group. For the Dominican government, hosting a CAM event and adhering to the IHRA definition serves four main purposes: it reaffirms its political subservience to US foreign policy, contributes to whitewashing the image of its ally Israel, portrays the Dominican regime as opposed to discrimination, and attempts to rewrite history to present the Trujillo dictatorship as the initiator of an alleged antidiscrimination policy upheld today by Abinader. There is indeed continuity between the Trujillo dictatorship and the current regime, but in a different sense. One Hand Washes the Other The statement from the Dominican foreign ministry announcing the adoption of the IHRA definition of antisemitism asserts that “the Dominican Republic underscores its ongoing commitment to the fight against all forms of hatred, discrimination, and religious intolerance, a position it has consistently maintained since 1938, when the Dominican state was the only one to offer asylum in Sosúa to a significant number of Jewish refugees.” The Dominican government goes on to urge all governments to take measures to “prevent hatred, intolerance, and discrimination in all their manifestations.” These are curious statements in light of Dominican history, not least the last six years of rule by Abinader’s right-wing Modern Revolutionary Party. That the Dominican government considers itself the heir to the Trujillo legacy is an important admission. President Abinader , named in the Pandora Papers leaks for having offshore accounts, has also admitted to sharing the ideas of dictator Joaquín Balaguer, who ruled the country with an iron fist from 1966 to 1978 and before that was one of the main ideologues and officials of the Trujillo regime. Since 2021, Abinader has been enforcing an undeclared state of exception to carry out mass deportations of Haitians, including the systematic use of arbitrary detentions based on racial profiling, raids without warrants, and militarization of hospitals and their use as immigration detention centers, as well as widespread violence by migration agents, including murders, torture, forced disappearances, and sexual violence. This article originally appeared in Jacobin , a democratic socialist magazine publishing long-form essays and analysis on politics, economics, and culture.
